## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Shāngzhǔ tiānzǐ suǒwèn jīng* (T591) is a one-fascicle Mahāyāna *devaputra-paripṛcchā* sūtra translated by Jñānagupta 闍那崛多 ([闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A)). *Shāngzhǔ* 商主 ("caravan-leader") renders Sanskrit *Sārthavāha*, a stock bodhisattva-epithet for the Buddha as guide of beings.

**Abstract**

A short Mahāyāna sūtra in question form on the bodhisattva path, datable to Jñānagupta's main translation period at Cháng'ān (591–600 CE) under the Suí Wéndì 隋文帝, when he served as leader of the imperial translation bureau at the Dà-xīngshàn 大興善 temple.
